questions.question: How should the integrand be interpreted?
options: It is the result of integrating, i.e. an antiderivative
It is the function being accumulated in an integral
It is the variable of integration named by $\mathrm{d}x$
It is the interval over which the values are accumulated

questions.question: Which part of an integral influences integrability?
options: The font used for the integral sign
Only the name of the variable
Properties of the integrand
Only the lower limit

questions.question: Which statement correctly identifies the integrand in both definite and indefinite integrals?
options: In both cases the integrand is the upper limit
In $\int_a^b f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$ and $\int f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$, the integrand is $f$
In both cases the integrand is the integral sign
In both cases the integrand is the final value of the integral

questions.question: In $\displaystyle\int_a^b f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$, what is not the integrand?
options: $f(x)$ as the function being accumulated
$\mathrm{d}x$
The function named by $f$

questions.question: Which mistake does $\displaystyle\int \,\mathrm{d}x$ help prevent?
options: Forgetting that with no function written, the integrand is $1$
Forgetting that the bounds are not part of the integrand
Forgetting that renaming $x$ as $t$ leaves an integral unchanged
Forgetting that an unbounded integrand can make an integral fail

questions.question: Why is the integrand more than a piece of notation?
options: It is always equal to the integral's numerical value
Its properties can influence whether the function is integrable
It fixes the antiderivative uniquely, with no additive constant needed
It sets the bounds of integration as well as the function

questions.question: A student says the integrand of $\displaystyle\int_0^1 x^2\,\mathrm{d}x$ is $[0,1]$. What is the correction?
options: The integrand is $\frac{x^3}{3}$; $[0,1]$ is the interval of integration
The integrand is $x$; $[0,1]$ is the interval of integration
The integrand is $x^2$; $[0,1]$ is the interval of integration
The integrand is $\frac{1}{3}$; $[0,1]$ is the interval of integration

questions.question: In $\displaystyle\int f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$, what is the integrand?
options: In $\displaystyle\int f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$, the integrand is $\mathrm{d}x$
In $\displaystyle\int f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$, the integrand is $f$
In $\displaystyle\int f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$, the integrand is the integral sign
In $\displaystyle\int f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$, the integrand is always $x$

questions.question: In an integral, what role does the integrand play?
options: It is the function being accumulated
It is the differential $\mathrm{d}x$ at the end
It is the number the integral produces
It is the pair of bounds $a$ and $b$

questions.question: Which part of $\displaystyle\int_a^b f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$ is the integrand?
options: $\mathrm{d}x$ alone

questions.question: In $\displaystyle\int \sin x\,\mathrm{d}x$, what is the integrand?
options: $\sin x$
$\mathrm{d}x$
$\int$

questions.question: Why do properties of the integrand matter?
options: They influence whether the function is integrable
They change only the name of the integration variable
They matter for indefinite integrals but not definite ones
They affect the value, but never whether it exists

questions.question: A student says the integrand of $\displaystyle\int_0^1 x^2\,\mathrm{d}x$ is $\mathrm{d}x$. What is correct?
options: The integrand is $0$
The integrand is $x^2$
The integrand is $1$
The integrand is $[0,1]$
